brief: Global equity flows turned net sold this week versus net bought last week, led by US and EM Asia; US Tech was the most net sold sector after leading inflows in 4 of the past 5 weeks, with a software to semis rotation and Mag7 positioning at a record 22% of US exposure versus 14% in June. On European stress, GS does not expect a systemic crisis given ECB backstop capacity, thinks ~40bp of tightening substitutes for one hike, and still calls a third and final ECB hike in December; European equities are down 5.7% off peak but EPS upgrades and a 5.5% FCF yield argue for buying Technology, Banks, Renewables, Defense and Capital intensive names. For US 3Q earnings, the Street sees growth decelerating to 27% YoY (GS: 9% median stock), but accelerating cloud growth supports >15% ROIC on AI capex and a 12m SPX target of 8700, with record issuance offset by higher buybacks. GS expects equities to bottom 2-3 months after the first hike, aligning with midterms, and keeps dry powder for after. In Asia, hedge funds sold for a 4th month, led by Korea Tech, even as GS argues the long run re-rating case stays intact.
